html:
The siege of Cartagena de Indias in 1741 was a failed attack by a large British fleet and army on the Spanish port of Cartagena, in today's Colombia, during the War of Jenkins' Ear.

Admiral Edward Vernon arrived in March with over a hundred ships and tens of thousands of men. The Spanish commander, Blas de Lezo, a one-legged, one-armed and one-eyed veteran, had only a few thousand defenders, but the city's forts and walls slowed the British. Yellow fever and dysentery killed British soldiers by the thousands, and an assault on the fortress of San Felipe failed.

In May the British withdrew. Cartagena and the coast of New Granada remained Spanish, and Spain kept its hold on its American empire for another seventy years. Blas de Lezo, who died soon after, is a hero in Spain and Colombia.
